ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: On the left side of the figure is an ideal operational amplifier. Its inverting input terminal is connected to a 100 kΩ resistor fed back from the output terminal and a grounded 10 kΩ resistor, forming a negative-feedback voltage-divider network; the non-inverting input terminal is connected from the 240 mV voltage source at the lower left through an input resistor. The op-amp output is labeled UO1, and is connected through a 5.1 kΩ resistor to the base of the transistor on the right; the transistor emitter is grounded, and the collector is connected through a 1 kΩ resistor to +15 V. Reasoning: According to the specified method, identify the op-amp part as a non-inverting amplifier. The ideal op-amp input current is 0, therefore there is no voltage drop across the input resistor at the non-inverting input terminal, and the voltage at the non-inverting terminal is 240 mV, namely 0.240 V. In the feedback network at the inverting terminal, the feedback resistor is 100 kΩ, and the grounded resistor is 10 kΩ, so the closed-loop gain of the non-inverting amplifier is 1 + 100 kΩ / 10 kΩ = 11. Therefore UO1 = 11 × 0.240 V = 2.64 V, and according to the precision expected by the problem, it is taken as approximately 2.6 V.
